steps.title: Identify the problem being compared
steps.explanation: The chapter’s static manufactured solution and this viewer’s implicit step are different experiments. Here both displayed meshes use the same quadratic-case loads and start with zero displacement and velocity for a 0.5 ms step.
steps.observe: The teal reference converges to its 4.16e-11 N target; the one-sweep orange solve has residual about 0.0438889 N. Geometry uses the same 20-fold displacement scale.

steps.title: Change only the order of one sweep
steps.explanation: Reverse strain-constraint traversal while retaining the mesh, material, load and sweep count. A finite sequential iteration can depend on the order in which it updates coordinates.
steps.observe: One reverse sweep uses the same 288 visits but gives residual about 0.0528295 N and maximum nodal difference 8.16060 µm. A sweep count is not an error bound.

steps.title: Resolve this finite-iteration difference
steps.explanation: Return to forward order and allow 20 sweeps. Compare the physical residual and error against the independent PCG result before calling the approximation resolved.
steps.observe: Relative objective-norm error is about 8.98e-11, and the compliant residual is about 2.90e-11 N. These are finite-mesh, small-strain results; they do not establish mesh convergence or large-rotation validity.

audit.finding: The chapter adapter did not distinguish its dynamic implicit fixture from the chapter’s static manufactured solution or expose finite-order sensitivity.
audit.change: Label the exact shared implicit problem and compare forward, reverse and resolved iterations using unscaled diagnostics.
audit.remaining: The viewer remains a fixed n=2 small-strain discretization. Static manufactured-solution refinement lives in the original chapter evidence; no transfer to nonlinear tissue, locking or anatomical calibration.
